California Chevrolet Dealer Sells New 2027 Corvette ZR1 Convertible 3LZ ZTK for $15,000 Over MSRP
25 photos
Photo: Bring a Trailer
If you're in the market for a flagship Corvette and you'd like to expedite your purchase, you're going to be paying over MSRP regardless. Meaning it doesn't matter whether it's a private seller or a dealer, or even a dealership. Case in point, this 2027 ZR1 Convertible, which was delivered new to AV Chevrolet of Lancaster, California with an MSRP of $267,284.
Fast-forward to last week, and this thing exchanged hands at auction for $282,284, basically $15,000 over MSRP - although keep in mind there's also a buyer's fee at play here, so technically the car cost more than $282k. Just saying.
There's an interesting parallel here between this ZR1 and another one that sold for $14,000 over MSRP back in January. That one was also a 3LZ Convertible, albeit without the ZTK Performance Track package. Still, it had $43,000 worth of optional extras, and it ended up selling for $257,000. Delivery miles were a given on both cars, by the way.
Is this particular ZR1 worth $25k more than the other one? Maybe. It depends on who you ask. It's got $49,000 worth of options. But let's take a closer look at the spec, starting with that black, Batmobile-like exterior.
Highlights also include a multitude of carbon fiber aero elements (rear wing, hood spoiler, dive planes, ground effects), a carbon fiber power-retractable hardtop, LED headlights, a front-axle lift system, plus a set of carbon fiber 20" and 21" wheels rocking Michelin rubber (Pilot Sport Cup 2) and silver-finished carbon-ceramic calipers. I gotta say, the wheels look amazing, and I love how the silver calipers blend into the discs like that. Surprisingly elegant for such an aggressive-looking supercar.
Meanwhile, inside is where you'll find the heated, ventilated and power-adjustable GT2 bucket seats trimmed in Adrenaline Red leather, plus you've got carbon fiber trim accents, ZR1 door-sill covers, keyless entry, dual-zone automatic climate control, cruise control, a Bose sound system, the Stealth Interior Trim Package, a heated and carbon-fiber trimmed steering wheel, a head-up display, and a wide array of electronic driver aids.
Photo: Bring a Trailer What's truly special about the ZR1 is its mid-mounted twin-turbocharged 5.5-liter LT7 V8 engine, pushing 1,064 horsepower and 828 lb-ft of torque to the rear wheels via an eight-speed dual-clutch automatic gearbox.
On paper, this thing will get you from zero to 60 mph (97 kph) in just 2.3 seconds (with a 1-foot rollout), before maxing out at 233 mph (375 kph). The C8 ZR1 is so close to being a 400 kph (249 mph) car, it's downright ridiculous - much like its prowess over a quarter mile, a distance it can "defeat" in about 9.6 seconds.
Ultimately, the C8 ZR1 is a $200k+ / sub-$300k, 9-second supercar with modern tech and daily drivability. What more could you want? Don't say a ZR1X! Or go ahead and say it. Both options make just as much sense.
